description.value:
Frequency once per day

Trigger You make a Strike using a weaponized Black Market cyber-augment.

You redline the augment the way you'd redline a scrap gun, and it answers the same way — bigger, once, and it costs you after. Treat the augment as one grade higher for that single Strike. Whether the Strike hits or not, you permanently gain +1 Drift when you do this — the augment doesn't forget being pushed, even if you never do it again.

cinderfall.incomplete: (Drift/augment-grade homebrew, same schema-uncertainty flag as integrated-iron). This card's entire effect is a limited-use activated action/reaction that hands the actor a wholly new usable action -- per this pass's fixed bucket-3 convention this is always INCOMPLETE regardless of precedent. Ironsight's own real-world analog, the Gunslinger, ships this exact shape unencoded across dozens of its own Strike-variant/reload-trick/called-shot feats (e.g. pf2e-source/packs/pf2e/feats/class/gunslinger/level-10/called-shot.json, level-6/scatter-blast.json, level-1/dual-weapon-reload.json, all rules: []) -- confirming this is the standard shape for a gunfighter class, not license to SKIP. This effect is defined entirely in terms of a Cinderfall-homebrew subsystem with zero Foundry schema footprint (the Gun Failure Table/Failure Range, hazardous ground, time-in-sights, Trick Iron charge bank, or Drift/augment-slot cost). Confirmed via the full rule-element type listing (pf2e-source/src/module/rules/rule-element/, 40 files): no RollTable-manipulation, no persistent-terrain-hazard, and no arbitrary stacking-counter rule element type exists to hook any of these to.
